the presence of functional groups and molecular size and weight of sodium humates (SH), isolated from soil, lignite, and compost are different.

the presence of functional groups (carboxyl in carbo- xylic acids, carbonyl in aldehyde and ketones, ether, and ester groups) in the order of samples of sodium humate isolated from compost, soil, and lignite are higher than in the sample of sodium humate from lignite.
the presence of functional groups (carboxyl, carbonyl, and hydroxyl groups) is in the order of soil > compost > lignite > lignohumates.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the samples of sodium humate isolated from the soil, compost, lignite, and commercial lignohumic acid are different in their chemical and structural composition.

the sample of sodium humate isolated from soil, lignite, and compost had a more complex and polycondensed structure, whereas the sample of commercial lignohumic acid had the most simple and low molecular weight.
lignohumate was a more condensed and aromatic substance, while compost was a more polycondense, oxidized, and unsaturated humic substance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lignite is a good source of humic acids (HA).

the sample of sodium humate from soil was characterized by a higher content of O-containing functional group, a more polycondensation, and aromaticity in comparison with the samples of sodium humate isolated from lignite, compost, and commercial LH.

the sample of lignohumate was characterized by the simplest structural components and wide heterogeneity of molecules, while the samples of sodium humate isolated from soil, lignite, and compost were characterized by more polycondensed aromatic structures.
